entries.meaning_it: Esclamazione di sorpresa, ammirazione, fastidio o disprezzo secondo l'intonazione; da 'pene'.
entries.meaning_en: All-purpose exclamation (surprise, admiration, annoyance, contempt); literally 'dick'.
entries.notes: Palermoviva (low): surprise, admiration, annoyance. Wiktionary: vulgar intj of surprise, disdain or appreciation. Keep out of formal contexts.

entries.meaning_it: Esclamazione di meraviglia o preoccupazione davanti a qualcosa di incredibile, buffo o disastroso.

examples.text: Bedda matri, u server è tuttu rossu!
examples.translation_it: Madonna, il server è tutto rosso!
examples.translation_en: Good grief, the server is all red!

entries.notes: Not a blasphemy in the sources, but an invocation of the Virgin; avoid in religious jokes.

entries.meaning_it: Esclamazione di stupore o meraviglia, versione più educata di minchia.
entries.meaning_en: Mild exclamation of wonder (softer cousin of minchia).
entries.notes: Balarm: stupore, meraviglia; the euphemism link to minchia is the author's remark, not a documented etymology.

entries.meaning_it: Andiamo! Dai! Usato anche per invitare a smettere ('ma dai').
entries.meaning_en: Let's go! / come on! / cut it out!
entries.notes: Wiktionary attests amuninni 'let's go; come on'. Palermoviva gives the short form amunì for Palermo.

entries.meaning_en: Forget it / don't sweat it / who cares.

examples.translation_en: Forget it, I'll do it tomorrow.

entries.notes: Palermoviva presents it as a Palermitan 'mantra'; the verb is vulgar (futtiri) but the tone is relaxed.

entries.meaning_it: Poveretto; anche intercalare di compatimento o ironia. Femminile: mischina.
entries.meaning_en: Poor thing; also a filler of pity or irony.

examples.translation_it: Poveretto, non ce la fa più.
examples.translation_en: Poor guy, he can't manage anymore.

entries.notes: Wiktionary (adj/noun) 'wretched, pitiful'. Balarm also reports a second sense, 'sly person', and the verb mischiniari; not used here.
Balarm quotes 'Talè come s'annaca' (mixed Italian/Sicilian).

entries.meaning_it: Esclamazione volgare dai molti sensi: scherno, rivalsa, vittoria, rifiuto; a Palermo anche scritta sui muri.
entries.meaning_en: Vulgar all-purpose retort ('suck it'): mockery, triumph, refusal.
entries.notes: Imperative of sucari. Wiktionary tags it vulgar slang. Between friends it is banter; never aim it at the user.

examples.text: Tu canziati, ca passa u cammiuni!
examples.translation_en: Move, the truck is coming through!

entries.notes: Palermoviva: 'tu canziati!' = move away urgently. Form given as printed.

entries.meaning_it: Amico, conoscente: vocativo confidenziale tipico della Sicilia occidentale.
entries.meaning_en: Friendly vocative 'buddy, mate', widespread in western Sicily.
entries.notes: Wiktionary: cumpà = alt form of cumpari (friend, buddy). Palermoviva: 'widespread especially in Western Sicily'. Catanese 'mbari is a different vocative (see profile §14).

entries.meaning_it: E che c'entra? Che discorsi sono? Si dice di chi dice cose fuori luogo o senza nesso.
entries.meaning_en: 'What's that got to do with anything?' / what nonsense are you saying.

examples.text: Chi nicchi e nacchi mi cunti?
examples.translation_en: What nonsense are you telling me?

entries.meaning_it: È andata malissimo, è finita nel peggiore dei modi.
entries.meaning_en: It went as badly as it could.

examples.text: Cu stu deploy muriu u cani.
examples.translation_it: Con questo deploy è finita malissimo.
examples.translation_en: With this deploy everything went to hell.

entries.meaning_it: È finita male (equivalente di 'muriu u cani').
Senza pretese, alla buona, in modo informale.
Ma che dici? Ma che stai raccontando?
entries.meaning_en: What the hell are you talking about?

examples.translation_en: What the hell are you saying?

entries.notes: Attested as a quoted example in the Balarm column (spelling as printed).

entries.meaning_it: Torno a casa, mi ritiro (dopo la misura è colma).
entries.notes: Palermoviva uses it in a gloss on camurria; form from that page.

entries.meaning_it: Assaggialo! Provalo (detto dai venditori dei mercati).
Assaggiare; a Palermo anche 'provare, mettere alla prova' con tono rituale.
entries.meaning_en: To taste, to try (a little ritual in Palermo markets).

entries.meaning_it: Lo distruggo, ne faccio polpette (minaccia di rabbia, spesso scherzosa).
entries.notes: Quoted in a Balarm column as an outburst; spelling as printed. Keep to objects or banter.
Struppiarsi = to get scraped or slightly hurt (as glossed by the source; Italian/Sicilian mixed).

entries.meaning_en: To let go, to give up on.
entries.notes: Seen only as 'ti lassasti ire' in a Balarm column; meaning inferred from context.
Imperative of annacarisi; Balarm gives the sense 'sbrigati'.

entries.meaning_it: Muoviti, non perdere tempo (imperativo di arriminarisi); in cucina 'mescola'.
entries.meaning_en: Get a move on! (also 'stir' in the kitchen).
entries.notes: Balarm: arriminarsi = mescolare; riferito a una persona, esortazione a sbrigarsi.

entries.meaning_it: Andare dritto per la propria strada, senza giri di parole.
entries.meaning_en: To go straight along one's way, no detours.
entries.notes: Cassaro = the straight main street of old Palermo (today Corso Vittorio Emanuele), per the source.

entries.term: nun mi cuntari li tri jorna du fistinu
entries.meaning_it: Non raccontarmi frottole né cose che so già.
entries.meaning_en: Don't tell me tall tales (or what I already know).
entries.notes: Refers to the three days of the Festino of Santa Rosalia (source).

entries.meaning_it: Gridare per vendere la merce, come nei mercati storici di Palermo.

entries.notes: Balarm: acchianata = the pilgrimage climb for Santa Rosalia.

entries.meaning_en: to put out, to switch off
entries.notes: Balarm uses the pair addumari/astutari (turn on/off) as a false friend with Italian astuto.
Wiktionary lists picciriddu as a variant spelling of picciriḍḍu; Balarm (Palermo) writes the plural picciriddi.
Wiktionary tags it also archaic/'young worker'. Use sparingly: Palermo is also reported to use picciotto, which was not checked.
Palermoweb writes masculine cucchiaru in the proverb 'u cucchiaru ca l'arrimina'.
Balarm (Palermo) uses 'noi granni' for adults as opposed to picciriddi.

entries.meaning_it: fissato, fuori di testa (fissato con qualcosa che non avverrà)
entries.notes: Derived from minchia; see profanity.json.
Wiktionary also lists a medical sense; the everyday sense is 'nuisance'.

entries.meaning_en: to sway; to dawdle; hurry up (imperative)

entries.meaning_it: abbellire, preparare a festa; sistemare alla meglio
entries.meaning_en: to dress up, to spruce up; to fix up

entries.meaning_it: rovinare (qualcosa che andava bene) con un intervento
entries.meaning_en: to spoil something that was fine
entries.notes: Balarm (Palermo): sminnari/sminnittiari = ruin; the folk etymology about weaning is flagged by the author as unverified.

entries.meaning_it: vendetta; distruzione ('fari minnitta' = ridurre in poltiglia)
persona sgradevole che approfitta dei privilegi a danno altrui

entries.notes: Palermo's Vucciria market gives the word; the source uses 'picca vucciria' for 'little noise'.
Seen once in a Balarm column ('stavo tampasiando con un mio amico'); sense inferred.
Plural used in 'inquietare i cristiani' (to bother people).
Palermoweb: 'u cani chi duormi' (diphthongised stressed vowel).
See profanity.json.
Only a headline on PalermoWeb was seen; included as local-culture vocabulary, low confidence.
Wiktionary lists both arancinu and arancina; the usual claim that Palermo says arancina (f.) and Catania arancinu (m.) was not source-checked here.
